CLOSED ON THE READ SIDE, WHICH IS THE WHOLE OF WHAT THAT FACT MEASURED. It named the fix in its own last line — "a rule that walks every property declared `node_ref` and reports an unresolvable value on its own terms, independent of the node's degree" — and that is what `dangling_reference` is, reusing `declared_node_refs` exactly as the fact suggested so the detector and the write guard cannot disagree about what a reference is.

🛑 ITS STATED SCOPE IS NOT CLOSED WITH IT, and must not be read as closed. The fact says plainly it was "measured on ONE property (`TemporalFact.subject_id`) on ONE graph" and that whether other types declare `node_ref`, and whether any of those dangle, was NOT measured. The new rule is written against the SCHEMA rather than against that one property, so it would find those too — but nobody has run it on a graph that has any, and a rule that would catch something is not the same fact as a measurement that nothing is there. On reflow2's own graph `subject_id` is still the only declared `node_ref`, so this design cannot supply the evidence.

WHAT ELSE THE MEASUREMENT KEEPS: its numbers (9 dangling, 7 reported, 2 silent), its mechanism sentence, and its observation that the bias ran the wrong way — an edgeless node being the least consequential place for a broken pointer. That last is now recorded as the reason the rule ignores degree, so it outlived the defect it explained.
